[SOURCE id=issue:567:567-summary:1255c28909d7 kind=issue issue=567 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#567.txt]
Issue: 567
Summary: On the latest master branch of OpENer, the report describes a remotely reachable server-side crash triggered by a crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request. The report attributes the underlying corruption to request handling before the visible crash: CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure() accepts a malformed CPF with an invalid item_count/inconsistent length, the unconnected Message Router payload reaches GetAttributeList(), GetAttributeList() parses an attacker-controlled excessively large attribute_count_request and builds an oversized inner Message Router response, and EncodeMessageRouterResponseData() copies that inner response into the outer ENIPMessage without validating remaining destination capacity. According to the report, this overruns message_buffer[512] and overwrites the adjacent current_message_position field; the observed result is that AddIntToMessage() later dereferences the corrupted pointer and crashes. The documented crash is an AddressSanitizer SEGV caused by a READ in AddIntToMessage() at source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c:136.
Reproduce: 1) Use the latest master branch of OpENer and run a server instance; the report demonstrates the issue on an AddressSanitizer-instrumented POSIX OpENer build. 2) Send the provided crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request to the server. The PoC is the hex byte sequence beginning with <6f><00><30><01><30><30><30><30> and continuing exactly as provided in the document. 3) Observe the server abort under AddressSanitizer with a SEGV caused by a READ in AddIntToMessage() at source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c:136:49, with the stack including EncodeSockaddrInfoItemTypeId(), AssembleLinearMessage(), NotifyCommonPacketFormat(), HandleReceivedSendRequestResponseDataCommand(), and HandleReceivedExplictTcpData().
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:569:569-summary:84e873f1b910 kind=issue issue=569 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#569.txt]
Issue: 569
Summary: In OpENer current master branch, the real unconnected explicit-message path from `RegisterSession` through `SendRRData`/CPF to `SetAttributeSingle` reaches a settable attribute in the default build, but request-data length is not checked before `attribute->decode(...)` is invoked. A crafted request that passes path decoding triggers a server-side out-of-bounds read in the attribute decoder (`GetUintFromMessage` / `GetUsintFromMessage`), and ASan reports it as a stack-buffer-overflow read.
Reproduce: Run the provided Python 3 PoC against the default POSIX OpENer server on `127.0.0.1:44818`. The script opens a socket, sends `RegisterSession`, extracts the session id from the reply, then sends `SendRRData` containing a `SetAttributeSingle` CIP message (`0x10`) in a Null Address / Unconnected Data Item CPF. Use the built-in `tcpip13` target for TCP/IP interface instance 1 attribute 13, or `qos8` for QoS instance 1 attribute 8; the crafted path is padded with `path_size_words=235`. Expected result: ASan reports a `stack-buffer-overflow` read in `GetUintFromMessage` / `GetUsintFromMessage`, with the trace passing through `DecodeCipTcpIpInterfaceEncapsulationInactivityTimeout` and `SetAttributeSingle`.
[/SOURCE]

Reproduce: Run the provided Python PoC against an OpENer 2.3.0 (commit 76b95cf) POSIX run instrumented as shown in the `ASan` section; the PoC defaults are `--host 127.0.0.1 --port 44818 --attempts 5 --timeout 1.5`. [SOURCE id=issue:572:572-summary:4cac5b77f97f kind=issue issue=572 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#572.txt]
Issue: 572
Summary: In OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf, the real TCP explicit-message path on port 44818 (`RegisterSession` / `SendRRData`) can reach `SetAttributeList()` with a default-registered, non-settable `kCipShortString` attribute: Identity class, instance 1, attribute 7 (`product_name`). For non-settable attributes, `SetAttributeList()` still advances over the attacker-supplied value, and for variable-length types it calls `GetCipDataTypeLength(attribute->type, message_router_request->data)` without validating remaining length. For `kCipShortString`, that leads to an unchecked 1-byte read via `GetSintFromMessage()`. With a long padded EPath positioning `message_router_request->data` at the end of the 512-byte stack receive buffer, ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read. The document states this is at minimum a remote unauthenticated denial of service in the default build.
Reproduce: Use OpENer v2.3 / master up to commit 76b95cf with the default Ethernet buffer size (`PC_OPENER_ETHERNET_BUFFER_SIZE=512`). Start the server, then run the provided Python 3 PoC in `crash` mode against TCP port 44818 (default host `127.0.0.1`, override with `OPENER_HOST`). The script first sends `RegisterSession`, then `SendRRData` carrying a CIP `SetAttributeList` request to Identity class 1, instance 1, attribute 7. In crash mode it builds a long padded EPath (`build_path(233)`) and sends `attr_count=1`, `attr=7`, with no short-string length byte following the attribute id. Expected result: ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read when `SetAttributeList()` skips the non-settable short string value.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:575:575-summary:e8df4ac3993c kind=issue issue=575 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#575.txt]
Issue: 575
Summary: OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit 76b95cf has a remotely reachable stack-use-after-return in the EtherNet/IP Common Packet Format (CPF) handling logic. The process-global CPF parsing state `g_common_packet_format_data_item` is reused across messages and protocol paths; `CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure()` only refreshes `data_item` when `item_count >= 2`, so a later CPF packet with `item_count == 1` updates only the address item and leaves the previous `data_item.type_id`, `data_item.length`, and `data_item.data` unchanged. A valid UDP I/O consuming packet can therefore populate `g_common_packet_format_data_item.data_item.data` with a pointer into the stack buffer of `CheckAndHandleConsumingUdpSocket()`, and a later TCP `SendUnitData` packet with only a `ConnectionAddress` item can reuse that stale UDP `data_item` in the TCP connected explicit path, causing `NotifyConnectedCommonPacketFormat()` to read from a returned UDP stack frame. The documented result on ASan builds is an `AddressSanitizer: stack-use-after-return` crash in `GetUintFromMessage`; the report states this is at minimum a remotely triggerable denial of service.
Reproduce: Use the unmodified POSIX OpENer server from v2.3 / master up to commit `76b95cf`; for the shown diagnostic, use an ASan build.
